stories.title: Nutty and the Basket of What-Ifs
stories.outro: See you next time in Sunny Meadow!
stories.moral: One useful plan can help more than trying to prevent every what-if.
moralRhyme: Pack what helps, then take a try,
Not each what-if needs a reply!

youtube.title: Nutty and the Basket of What-Ifs | Sunny Meadow
youtube.description: Nutty's picnic basket was too full to lift. Grandpa Tilly waited beside a mountain of extra things. A gentle friendship story. One useful plan can help more than trying to prevent every what-if. #SunnyMeadow #DreamyDiscoveries

lines.text: Nutty's picnic basket was too full to lift.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Grandpa Tilly waited beside a mountain of extra things.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: What if we need all this while we are out?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: We seem to have packed for several very different picnics.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty had wanted a peaceful afternoon in the meadow.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now his plans felt bigger than the little basket.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: What if the ground is wet or the wind blows?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Those are possibilities. Which things will help us today?
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty added a second cloth beneath the first.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then he packed a cushion for every imagined damp spot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now we can sit somewhere dry on every side.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And the basket has become much harder to carry.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty tied three spare bags around the wooden handle.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He filled them with things for more imaginary problems.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: What if we drop a spoon, or lose the cloth?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: We can manage a small problem without packing the whole room.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Does Nutty need to pack everything he owns?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The handle leaned beneath Nutty's extra little bags.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He could not move the picnic away from the bench.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Perhaps we should stay here and cancel going anywhere.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Would that be the afternoon you wanted to have?
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty looked toward the meadow through the open park gate.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He still wanted the simple picnic he had imagined.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I wanted lunch beside the grass, not all this worrying.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Then let us choose what helps that small plan.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty unpacked the spare bags and three extra cushions.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He set them neatly beside their usual storage basket.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Food, water, and one cloth will do the main jobs.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: What will you do if a small surprise happens?
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty considered a breeze lifting one corner of the cloth.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He placed one smooth pebble beside their picnic things.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I can hold the corner down if it flaps.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: That is one useful answer to one likely little problem.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty closed the basket after checking the drinking water.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: There was room around the things he actually needed.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I still have some what-ifs in my head.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: They can come along without filling every part of the basket.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: What belongs in a simple picnic plan?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: They walked through the gate onto the meadow path.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Nutty carried the light basket in both front paws.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: My picnic finally has room to leave the bench.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And we have room to notice the afternoon around us.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: They spread the cloth where the ground felt dry.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: One loose corner fluttered in a very gentle breeze.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Here is the small surprise I made a plan for.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Your smooth pebble can help while we sit down.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty set the pebble on the fluttering cloth corner.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The other edge stayed still beneath his own basket.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: That worked. I did not need six extra cushions.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Now your lunch can come out instead of more equipment.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Nutty noticed a tiny leaf drop beside his cup.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He moved it onto the grass without making another plan.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I did not pack anything for a leaf visitor.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You handled that small surprise with the paw you brought.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: They ate their picnic beneath the mild meadow sky.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Nutty glanced at his pleasantly light basket and smiled.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: My biggest problem was bringing too many solutions.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: At least your spare cushions are having a comfortable day home.
lines.speaker: friend
